How I'd explain
Machine Learning

slides.sub:
12 ideas from one school day.
The real Python under each.

cells.kid: Your class register. Every row is one child, every column is one fact about them.
The clues you look at before guessing: height, age, how fast you run.
The answer you want to guess, like who wins the school race.
Show a child many mango pictures until they can spot a mango alone.
You see dark clouds in the morning, so you pack an umbrella for school.
Teacher keeps some questions hidden for the final exam, not the practice sheet.
Sort every sweet into one of two boxes: chocolate or not chocolate.
Guess how many runs your team will score. A number, not a box.
At lunch, kids make their own groups. Nobody tells them who sits where.
Twenty questions game. Is it red? Is it round? Then it is an apple.
Out of 10 spelling words, you wrote 8 correctly. That is 80 percent.
Mugging up the answer key. Full marks in practice, lost in the real exam.
